subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the next steps we discussed so everything is aligned on our side. Feel free to correct anything I missed.

Pain points you highlighted:
- Rapidly rising inference spend (token/unit economics) as usage scales — current monthly spend up ~3x YoY and trending higher.
- Latency sensitivity for customer-facing flows (p95 target you mentioned ~200ms).
- Inconsistent batching and no KV prefix caching in current stack leading to wasted compute.
- Concerns about model quality degradation if aggressive quantization is applied.

Current stack (what you told us):
- Self-hosted on cloud VMs (NVIDIA T4/G4 equivalent) managed by your infra team.
- Using an ONNX-based pipeline for most models; some custom batching but no centralized batching service.
- No production KV cache today; short-term experiments only.

Success criteria you specified:
1) Reduce per-inference unit cost by ~40-50% (target: half of current unit economics) while preserving >98% of current QoR on key prompts.
2) Meet p95 latency <= 200ms for critical flows at expected concurrency (you noted peaks around 150-250 rps).
3) Minimal integration effort — prefer solutions that can slot into current infra (VPC/private deployment) and support SOC 2 requirements.

Openness to optimizations:
- You’re open to quantization (int8 or mixed) for non-critical models if we can demonstrate minimal quality regression.
- Interested in batching + prefix/KV caching as primary levers to reduce token compute.

Immediate next steps (agreed):
1) I’ll share an initial pricing estimate and a short discovery notes doc (attached).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Dev and Marissa to walk throughput/latency contours and pilot architecture (aiming for Wednesday/Thursday this week).
3) If the deep-dive looks good, we’ll propose a 30-day pilot on Redwood Dedicated with a scoped SLA and success metrics.

Attachments: discovery-notes-fintechcorp.docx (discovery notes), redwood-initial-pricing-estimate.pdf (pricing snapshot)

If that all aligns, I’ll send calendar options for the deep-dive. Thanks again — excited to dig in.

Best,
Ben Carter

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Thanks Ben — this is a good summary and captures the main points. A few clarifications/questions from our side: 

1) Peak concurrency: we see short spikes up to ~250 rps but steady-state at ~120-160 rps. Any pricing estimates should call out peak vs. steady-state assumptions.
2) Quantization: willing to try int8 for internal models, but for customer-facing summarization we need to maintain current ROUGE/BLEU-equivalent quality (we have a few guarded prompts). Would you be able to run quality regressions on a small prompt set?
3) Pilot timeline: we’d prefer a pilot that can start by end of month (Jun 30) and run for ~30 days.
4) Compliance: we require SOC 2 and prefer VPC deployment; please note this in the proposal.

Also looping in Priya from procurement (priya.singh@fintechcorp.com) to keep her in the loop on procurement timing once we have a pricing snapshot.

Can you include a short breakdown of expected cost savings from batching vs. quantization vs. caching? Even ballpark numbers will help the execs.

Thanks — Sanjay

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Thanks Sanjay — great questions. Couple of quick clarifications and a proposed plan to move forward: 

1) Pricing assumptions / breakdown (ballpark):
   - Batching improvements: expected 20-30% reduction in token compute for request patterns with variable lengths (we’ll need request histograms to refine).
   - Prefix/KV caching: can yield 15-35% savings on stateful, prompt-heavy flows (depends on cache hit rate; we typically see 25%+ for chat-style UXs).
   - Quantization (int8/mixed): typically 20-40% CPU/GPU efficiency improvement on throughput for large transformer layers; quality regression varies—we’ll run prompt-set regressions to quantify.
   - Combined (batching + caching + quantization): conservative combined estimate ~45% cost reduction; aggressive tuning can exceed 60% on some workloads.

2) Pilot proposal and timeline:
   - Technical deep-dive (60-90m) with Dev + Marissa to review traffic traces, latency contours, and VM/hardware mapping. Proposed slots: Wed 2026-06-17 10:00-11:30 PT or Thu 2026-06-18 14:00-15:30 PT. Please confirm which works.
   - Pilot: 30-day Dedicated capacity pilot starting target week of Jun 29- Jul 3. Scope: ingest 2 weeks of traffic, enable caching and batching + a quantization experiment on a non-critical model, track p50/p95 latency and per-token cost.
   - Success metrics: >=40% unit-cost reduction or a clear path to reach it within the pilot; p95 <=200ms on critical flows; <2% quality regression on guarded prompts for production models.

3) SOC 2 / Deployment: Redwood can provide a VPC/private deployment model and SOC 2 evidence. Marissa will follow up on SOC 2 artifacts and integration checklist.

4) Next actions (I’ll own):
   - Share a short pricing breakdown + the attached estimate (redwood-initial-pricing-estimate.pdf).
   - Schedule the technical deep-dive once you confirm a slot.
   - Marissa/Dev to scope required traces/artifacts we’ll need for the deep-dive.

Attachment: redwood-initial-pricing-estimate.pdf

If that looks good, I’ll lock the Wed slot and get calendar invites out.

Best,
